ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points A and B are on the graphs of the inverse proportion functions $y=\frac{2}{x}$ ($x>0$) and $y=\frac{4}{x}$ ($x>0$) respectively, and AB is parallel to the x-axis. If C is any point on the x-axis, then what is the area of $\triangle ABC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, extend BA to intersect the y-axis at point M, and connect OA, OB,\\
since line AB is parallel to the x-axis,\\
since $S_{\triangle AOM}=1$, $S_{\triangle BOM}=2$,\\
therefore $S_{\triangle ABC}=S_{\triangle ABO}=S_{\triangle BOM}-S_{\triangle AOM}=2-1=\boxed{1}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows two inverse proportional function curves in the first quadrant, point A is on the curve on the left side, point B is on the curve on the right side, line segment AB is horizontal and is located above the x-axis; point C is marked on the x-axis, and triangle ABC is represented by shading. Reasoning: Because AB is parallel to the x-axis, let the common y-coordinate of A and B be h, and h>0. A is on y=2/x, so h=2/x, obtaining A=(2/h,h). B is on y=4/x, so h=4/x, obtaining B=(4/h,h). Therefore the length of AB is 4/h-2/h=2/h. Since C is on the x-axis, the perpendicular distance from point C to the horizontal straight line AB, namely y=h, is h. So the area of triangle ABC is S=1/2×AB×h=1/2×(2/h)×h=1.
